translations.text: I, Ælfric, monk and mass-priest, though weaker than befits such orders, was sent in the days of King Æthelred by Bishop Ælfheah,
Æthelwold's successor, to a certain monastery which is called Cerne, at the request of Æthelmær the thegn, whose birth and goodness are known everywhere.
Then it came into my mind, I trust through God's grace, that I should turn this book from the Latin language into the English tongue;
not out of confidence in any great learning, but because I saw and heard much error in many English books, which unlearned people in their simplicity regarded as great wisdom;

and I was sorry that they did not know or have the teaching of the gospel in their writings, except for those people alone who knew Latin, and except for the books that King Alfred wisely translated from Latin into English, which are available.
For this reason I ventured, trusting in God, to undertake this composition, and also because people need good teaching most of all in this time, which is the ending of this world,
and there will be many perils among mankind before the end comes, just as our Lord said to his disciples in his gospel:
"Then there will be such tribulations as there never were before, from the beginning of the world."
Many false Christs will come in my name, saying, 'I am Christ,' and they will work many signs and wonders to deceive mankind, and even the chosen ones as well, if it can happen:
and unless the Almighty God shortened those days, all mankind would perish; but for the sake of his chosen ones he shortened the days."
Each person can the more easily withstand the coming temptation, through God's help, if he is strengthened by the teaching of books; for those will be saved who persevere in faith to the end.

Many afflictions and hardships will come upon this world before its ending, and they are the heralds of eternal destruction for evil people, who afterward will suffer eternally for their wicked deeds in dark hell.
Then the Antichrist will come, who will be a human man and a true devil, just as our Saviour is truly man and God in one person.
And the visible devil will then work countless wonders, and say that he himself is God, and will try to force mankind into his heresy;
but his time will not be long; for God's wrath will destroy him, and this world will afterward be ended.

Christ our Lord healed the infirm and the sick, and this devil who is called Antichrist, that is to say, contrary Christ, lames and weakens the healthy, and heals no one of infirmities except those alone whom he himself had injured before.
He and his followers will secretly injure men's bodies through the devil's craft, and heal them openly in people's sight; but he cannot heal anyone whom God himself has afflicted beforehand.
Through wickedness he compels people to turn from faith in their Creator to his lies, he who is the source of every lie and every evil.
The Almighty God will allow the wicked Antichrist to work signs and wonders and persecution for three and a half years;
for at that time there will be so much evil and perversity among mankind that they will well deserve the devilish persecution,
to eternal destruction for those who submit to him, and to eternal joy for those who oppose him through faith.
God also allows his chosen servants to be cleansed from all sins through the immense persecutions, just as gold is tested in fire.
Then the devil will kill those who resist him, and they will then go with holy martyrdom to the kingdom of heaven.
Those who believe his lies he will spare, and afterwards they will have eternal torment as the reward for their heresy.
The wicked one will make fire come down as if from heaven in people's sight, as though he were God Almighty, who has power over heaven and earth.
But Christians must then remember what the devil did when he asked God that he might test Job.
He then caused fire to come down as if from heaven, and it burned up all his sheep out in the field, and the shepherds as well, except one who was to tell him of it.
The devil did not send the fire from heaven, even though it came from above, because he himself was not in heaven after he had been cast down for his pride.
Nor does the cruel Antichrist have the power to send heavenly fire, even though through the devil's craft he may make it look that way.
It is now wiser that everyone should know this and know his faith, in case anyone should have to live through that great misery.
Our Lord commanded his disciples that they should instruct and teach all nations the things that he himself had taught them;
but there are now too few of those who are willing to teach well and set a good example. The same Lord cried out through his prophet Ezekiel:

"If you do not reprove [?] the unrighteous man, and do not admonish him to turn from his wickedness and live, then the wicked man will die in his unrighteousness, and I will require his blood of you," that is, his perdition.
"But if you warn the wicked man and he will not turn from his wickedness, you have delivered your soul by that warning, and the wicked man will die in his unrighteousness."
Again the Almighty said to the prophet Isaiah, "Cry out and do not cease; lift up your voice like a trumpet, and declare to my people their crimes, and to the household of Jacob their sins."
Because of such commands it seemed to me that I would not be guiltless before God if I were unwilling to make it known to other people, either by tongue or by writings,
the gospel truth that he himself spoke and afterwards revealed to holy teachers.
For I know a great many in this land more learned than I am, but God reveals his wonders through whomever he will.
As an almighty maker, he works his work through his chosen ones, not as though he needed our help, but so that we may earn eternal life through carrying out his work.
Paul the apostle said, "We are God's helpers," and yet we do nothing for God without God's help.
Now I ask and entreat in God's name that, if anyone wishes to copy this book, he correct it carefully against the exemplar, lest we be blamed because of careless scribes.
He who writes falsely does great evil, unless he corrects it; it is as if he turns the true teaching into false heresy:
Therefore everyone must set right what he has previously bent into error, if he wishes to be guiltless at God's judgment.
Why is it necessary to arrange chapter headings in this book, since we have already said that it contains forty discourses? Except that Ealdorman Æthelweard wanted to have forty-four in his book.
